Figure 3. Retrieval coverage of the union-trained all-pool portfolio. Curves are averaged over HotpotQA, MusiQue, TriviaQA, and 2WikiMultiHopQA. The all-pool curve evaluates greedy portfolio prefixes by best-of-k support score. The top-k average baseline selects the k retrievers with highest mean training score. The k× document baselines run one best retriever from a family while increasing its document budget from 4 to 4k.
Figure 2. Adaptive Inference Pipeline: The router encodes query q and identifies best portfolio members. Selected components execute in parallel to minimize latency, followed by selector aggregation.

Table 3. Answer Exact-Match (EM) across datasets and retrieval strategies for Gemma-3-27B-It and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. Best DS, Vendi, and GraphDense rows select the best single retriever by average performance. The reported Vendi-only portfolio point, (k=5, ℓ=2), and all-pool operating points, (k=4, ℓ=2) and (k=4, ℓ=3), are selected from their routed sweeps by average EM. Bold denotes the best value in each dataset/model column.
Figure 4. Efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Row 1: total generated tokens vs. EM. Row 2: wall-clock time vs. EM. Columns correspond to Gemma-3-27B-It and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct.
